column3: Exact repetition: Satan is the manifest enemy of humankind.
The straight path positively answers the focus's prohibited allegiance.
Shows Satan's first deceptive approach to Adam and his spouse.
Repeats the Satan-as-manifest-enemy formula in a warning to a son.
Within-surah cosmic order supplies only a distant order-versus-deviation contrast.
Commands worship of God alone and warns of punishment.
Repeats the warning against Satan's steps and his manifest enmity.
Immediate continuation: worship God; this is the straight path.
Names Satan as the enemy and commands treating him as such.
Addresses Adam's children and warns them not to be tempted by Satan.
Immediate continuation: Satan has led many astray from this charge.
Frames devils as enemies who deceive through embellished speech.
Directly commands worship of God alone.
Mentions punishment of wrongdoers without the focus's allegiance warning.
Covenant-keeping develops the focus's ahd dimension.
Addresses Adam's children with divine conduct commands, but not Satan.
Within-surah celestial ordering has no direct worship-or-enmity link.
Commands fulfillment of covenant, a clear ahd counterpart.
Addresses Adam's children with guidance, piety, and reform.
The scoffing at the promised event anticipates the surrounding judgment scene.
Rejects what others worship and turns exclusively to God.
Links Adam's fall to the explicit statement that Satan is a manifest enemy.
Deceptive listening by liars offers only a secondary Satanic-deception parallel.
A polemic over assigning daughters to God does not clarify the focus.
Adam's forgotten covenant gives a direct precedent for the charge to Adam's children.
Cosmic limits offer a distant order-and-boundary counterpart only.
Satan's service under Solomon does not clarify forbidden worship of Satan.
Rejects false worship and commands worship of God alone.
A believer's confession of faith provides limited within-surah support.
Human conflict with enemies is distinct from Satanic enmity.
A prophetic warning commands worship of God alone and fears punishment.
Sincere servants are excluded from Satan's misleading reach.
The rejected daughters-and-sons claim does not illuminate the focus.
Adam's repentance after receiving divine words complements the Adamic covenant frame.
Immediate continuation identifies the promised Hell as the consequence.
Ibrahim calls false objects of worship enemies, except the Lord.
Messengers command worship of God alone; rejection follows.
The sudden event's consequences continue the nearby judgment sequence.
Commands believers to worship God alone wherever they are.
Rules for a wartime group do not clarify Satanic worship or enmity.
Musa's request to glorify God has no focused connection.
Pairs worshippers with their objects of worship in a false-allegiance setting.
Addresses a people with covenant fulfillment and exclusive fear of God.
Immediate continuation commands entry into Hell for disbelief.
The battle-line construction image does not clarify the focus.
The messianic announcement to Israel does not clarify the focus.
A nearby sign of provision has no direct allegiance link.
Repeats the ban on Satan's steps and the manifest-enemy formula.
Broken promise and incurred wrath provide a covenant-warning parallel.
Musa's request to remember God has no focused connection.
Explicitly denies that devils brought down the revelation.
Calls named enemies of God and believers to account, in a military setting.
Loss of sight on the path develops the nearby misguidance sequence.
Ibrahim commands his people to worship God and be mindful of Him.
God's sole dominion and protection give a limited allegiance contrast.
Following rightly guided messengers is a limited within-surah path parallel.
God knows the believers' enemies and is sufficient protector.
Treaty and noncombatant rules do not clarify the focus.
Divine awareness in Musa's prayer has no focused connection.
Reckless construction is unrelated to the focus's warning.
The restoration of Yaqub's sight does not clarify the focus.
Immobility supplies only a distant within-surah contrast to following a path.
False objects of worship become enemies of their worshippers at gathering.
Commands following the best revelation before sudden punishment.
The ark sign does not clarify worship, covenant, or enmity.
States that jinn and humankind were created to worship God.
Destruction of earlier peoples gives a broad warning counterpart.
Mary and her son as a sign do not clarify the focus.
Transgression and wrongdoing lead to fire, without Satanic allegiance.
Praises those who faithfully guard trusts and covenants.
The surah's closing sovereignty and return frame the ultimate accountability.
Defines a recipient of mercy and knowledge first as God's servant.
Directly says not to worship Satan and identifies his rebellion against the Merciful.
The punishment of a rejecting town is only a nearby judgment parallel.
Prescribes refuge in God when Satan provokes.
Names Satan as humanity's manifest enemy and his divisive provocation.
Condemns worship of false powers and being led far from the right path.
Deliverance of Israel from humiliation has only a distant Adam's-children link.
Repeats the warning against Satan's steps and his manifest enmity.
The Messenger is established upon the straight path named in the continuation.
Calls Nuh one of God's believing servants, a positive worship identity.
Warns Adam's children against taking Iblis and his offspring as allies despite enmity.
The merciful greeting contrasts with the judgment that follows, but indirectly.
Explicitly denies that the revelation is Satanic speech.
Warns that becoming Satan's ally leads toward punishment.
Faithful reception of revelation is only a remote positive counterpoint.
The transgressing sinner supplies a limited moral counterpart to Satanic deviation.
Depicts devils inciting the disbelievers.
The divine Merciful revelation contrasts with Satanic influence.
The oath by the sky and its construction does not clarify the focus.
Disbelief and pride against revelation provide only a distant warning parallel.
At gathering, alleged worshippers are confronted with their objects of worship.
Household eating permissions do not clarify the focus.
Righteousness includes fulfilling covenants within an integrated faithfulness account.
Divorce waiting-period rules do not clarify the focus.
The mention of sons offers only a lexical Adam's-children echo.
Inheritance allocations for children do not clarify the focus.
Prohibits food dedicated to other than God, a related exclusive-allegiance boundary.
A battlefield ultimatum does not clarify Satanic worship or enmity.
Warns of hostile hypocrites, though not Satan or forbidden worship.
Iblis refuses the command concerning Adam, grounding the Adam-Satan opposition.
Satan causes Adam and his spouse to slip from their appointed state.
Devils teach what harms people, an explicit Satanic-deception parallel.
Jesus commands worship of God as Lord and identifies the straight path.
Calls to worship God alone and reject associating partners with Him.
Identifies Satan as one who frightens people through his allies.
Commands worship of God and forbids associating anything with Him.
Condemns seeking judgment from false powers while claiming belief.
Contrasts believers with the allies of Satan and calls Satan's plot weak.
Describes invoking others besides God as invoking a rebellious Satan.
Names Satan as cursed after his defiant claim over human beings.
Records Satan's program of leading people astray and commanding false alterations.
Satan promises and arouses desire while offering only delusion.
Rejects treating the Messiah as God and commands worship of God alone.
Questions worship of what has neither power to harm nor benefit.
Names wine and gambling Satan's work and commands avoiding them.
Satan seeks enmity and to turn people from God's remembrance and prayer.
The Prophet is forbidden to worship those invoked besides God.
Condemns making the jinn partners with God despite His sole creation.
Devils inspire their allies to dispute against divine guidance.
Commands not associating anything with God.
Declares prayer, sacrifice, life, and death wholly for God.
Places Iblis's refusal within the creation and command concerning Adam.
Records Iblis's prideful refusal to prostrate to Adam.
Iblis is expelled for arrogance and humiliation.
Iblis asks for respite, continuing the adversarial narrative.
God grants Iblis respite to an appointed time.
Iblis vows to obstruct people from God's straight path.
Iblis vows to approach people from every direction to mislead them.
Iblis and his followers are assigned the consequence of Hell.
Addresses Adam's children and ties piety to the divinely given covering.
A group is led astray after taking devils as allies instead of God.
Commands seeking refuge in God when Satan's prompting arises.
God-conscious people remember when touched by Satan and regain sight.
Condemns taking religious authorities as lords instead of worshipping one God.
Commands worship of God alone rather than what others worship.
Hud commands his people to worship God alone.
Salih commands his people to worship God alone.
Shuayb commands his people to worship God alone.
Satan causes forgetfulness, showing his obstructive influence.
Yusuf attributes the estrangement between brothers to Satan.
Satan disavows those who followed his promise and blames their response.
Iblis vows to make wrongdoing attractive and lead people astray.
God identifies a straight path over which He retains authority.
Satan has no authority over God's sincere servants, only over followers.
Commands worship of God and avoidance of false powers in every community.
Satan makes earlier peoples' deeds attractive to them.
Commands refuge in God before reciting against the accursed Satan.
Satan has no authority over believers who rely on their Lord.
Satan's authority applies to those who take him as patron and associate partners.
Commands worship of none but God.
Begins Iblis's refusal concerning Adam and his claim over Adam's progeny.
Iblis vows to seize nearly all of Adam's descendants.
God identifies Hell as the recompense for Iblis and his followers.
Details Satan's means of mobilizing and sharing in people's lives and wealth.
Limits Satan's authority over God's servants.
The companions declare that they will not worship any god besides their Lord.
God commands worship of Him alone and establishes prayer for remembrance.
Harun tells his people their Lord is the Merciful and commands following him.
Iblis refuses the command to prostrate to Adam.
Satan whispers to Adam and promises an enduring kingdom.
Links descent, mutual enmity, and divine guidance that protects from going astray.
Every messenger receives the command to worship God alone.
Condemns following every rebellious devil without knowledge.
Whoever takes the devil as ally is led astray toward the Blaze.
Satan attempts to cast interference into prophetic recitation.
Satanic interference becomes a test for diseased and hardened hearts.
Nuh commands his people to worship God alone.
A messenger commands his people to worship God alone.
Rejects any god alongside God or division of divine authority.
Condemns invoking another god beside God without proof.
Satan abandons the human being after causing deviation from remembrance.
Condemns taking one's own desire as a god.
Describes worship of what neither benefits nor harms, alongside rejection of God.
Introduces Ibrahim's confrontation with his people's worship.
Ibrahim asks his people what they worship.
The people identify the idols to which they remain devoted.
Satan makes sun worship attractive and bars a people from the path.
Musa identifies inciting wrongdoing as Satan's work.
Ibrahim calls idols false fabrications and commands worship of God.
Shuayb commands his people to worship God and await the Last Day.
Satan makes destructive deeds attractive and turns people from the path.
Luqman forbids associating partners with God as grave wrongdoing.
Following inherited practice is contrasted with Satan's call toward the Blaze.
Satan makes evil deeds attractive so that they appear good.
The deniers refuse the declaration that there is no god but God.
They reject abandoning false gods in response to the Messenger.
Introduces Adam's creation before the Iblis confrontation.
All angels prostrate, setting Iblis apart as the exception.
Iblis refuses and becomes arrogant among the disbelievers.
God confronts Iblis over refusing the command concerning Adam.
Iblis asserts false superiority over Adam as grounds for refusal.
Iblis is expelled and accursed for his defiance.
The curse upon Iblis endures until the Day of Recompense.
Iblis asks for respite until resurrection.
God grants Iblis respite to the appointed time.
Iblis swears that he will mislead human beings.
Iblis excepts God's sincere servants from his misleading claim.
God confirms the truth governing the Iblis narrative.
Hell is promised for Iblis and all who follow him.
Commands worship of God with religion made sincere for Him.
Rejects taking protectors besides God under a worship rationale.
Commands sincere worship of God.
The Prophet declares that he worships God with religion made sincere.
Praises those who avoid false powers and turn back to God.
Questions the power of those invoked besides God.
Rejects being commanded to worship other than God.
Warns that associating partners nullifies deeds and brings loss.
Commands worship of God alone and gratitude to Him.
Identifies God as creator and Lord, then commands worship of Him.
Commands upright devotion to the one God and seeking His forgiveness.
A person who turns from the Merciful is assigned a devil companion.
Devil companions bar people from the path while they think themselves guided.
Affirms that no gods besides the Merciful were appointed for worship.
Jesus brings wisdom and calls his people to be mindful of God.
Jesus commands worship of God as his Lord and theirs, the straight path.
Condemns taking personal desire as a god and following it despite knowledge.
Begins the critique of revered false deities.
Rejects named objects of worship as unsupported conjecture and desire.
Satan overwhelms people and makes them forget God's remembrance.
Satan commands disbelief, then disavows the one who obeys him.
Ibrahim's community disavows those who worship besides God.
Commands that no one be invoked alongside God in places of worship.
Commands sincere worship of God, upright prayer, and almsgiving.
Names the whisperer who withdraws as the evil to be sought refuge from.
Identifies the whispering activity within human hearts.
Identifies whisperers as among jinn and humankind.
